verify:
 # SPEC-0152 rule 16. The per-layer LAND-VERIFY carrier — `verify.layers` is the AUTHORITATIVE
 # land-layer universe. DECLARE a `layers:` list (each { layer: <id>, command: <hermetic land cmd> }
 # OR { layer: <id>, waiver: {reason} }; optional `covers:` globs) OR WAIVE the whole concern (a
 # LOOSE bare `reason:`). A legacy yitc-verify.yaml is folded into this section at init.
 # HERMETIC — `land` runs each `command:` on the LIVE host — isolated project, ephemeral ports, never
 # mutating prod/host state (no shared DB, no fixed host ports, no `down -v` on a live stack); a
 # non-hermetic command makes `land` destructive.
 # Optional `subject_globs:` lets a land whose diff is DISJOINT from them skip the layer (absent ⇒
 # always runs). Author them from a DEPENDENCY AUDIT of the layer's command (its real reads, mounts,
 # sub-scripts) — NOT by copying `covers:`; declare a SUPERSET of it.
 # Container shape — choose it KNOWINGLY and write the reason in the layer comment:
 # - THROWAWAY: each probe brings up and tears down its own container (`compose run --rm`).
 # - EXEC: the layer brings a stack up ONCE and each probe runs inside it (`compose exec`).
 # see SPEC-0152 §16; SPEC-0093 §3
 # TIMEOUT (X-0204). Per layer `timeout: <seconds>` and/or section `timeout_seconds:`;
 # in precedence order: the env escape hatch (YITC_VERIFY_TEST_TIMEOUT) · layer · section · the 300s
 # default;
 # a malformed value fails the land CLOSED.
 # HOW TO CHOOSE THE NUMBER: SPEC-0208 (`bin/yitc-v2 graph query SPEC-0208`) — measure p95 by nearest
 # rank (n >= 20) under the tuple you land under, declare inside [2 x p95, 4 x p95], record it here.
 waiver:
 reason: "Initialized via `bin/yitc-v2 init` — no land-verify layer declared yet; declare a `layers:` list (each {layer, command} or per-layer {layer, waiver:{reason}}) as this project's land-verify layers settle (SPEC-0152 rule 16)."

gated_capabilities.absent: every land is verified alone — batches of one, whatever the queue depth.
gated_capabilities.summary: land-verify BATCHING — several queued lands verified TOGETHER, in ONE pass over a combined candidate, instead of a full verify per land. Declare it only if your layers isolate one change from another: a shared fixture, port, database or build cache can make one member's failure indistinguishable from a peer's, which is why the kernel cannot infer this.

gated_capabilities.absent: every declared layer runs serially, in declaration order — the verify wall is their sum.
gated_capabilities.summary: CONCURRENT land-verify layers — the layers named here run OVERLAPPED in one land instead of one after another (the wall drops from their sum towards their longest). YOU decide, and you bear the risk: naming layers here is your project's own risk judgement. The kernel checks the shape of the list only and never polices independence, so a wrong declaration costs only your own verify. Before declaring, check each named pair, their `prep:` included, against every resource class two layers can collide on: mutable_files, caches, temp_paths, services, locks, processes, shared_sinks. A per-layer `owns:` declaration is an optional aid for that check, never a requirement. Fail-fast, per-layer timeouts and the per-layer rows are unchanged; a name matching no declared layer fails the land closed.

gated_capabilities.absent: every layer reads the whole allotment — unsplit, as today.
gated_capabilities.summary: HOW YOU SPLIT the land's worker allotment across your layers — a mapping of layer name to that layer's FRACTION (a number in (0, 1], never a core count, so a change to the kernel's allotment re-splits automatically and nothing here is rewritten). The kernel declares the form, validates it, records each share beside the CPU that layer actually consumed, and keeps publishing the WHOLE allotment in YITC_VERIFY_LAYER_WORKERS; it computes nothing and publishes no per-layer number. YOU split it and scale your own runners — only you know what your layers do. The sum is deliberately unchecked: there is no over-allocation guard, and a share that floors at one worker is your arithmetic.

 # waiver. The waiver is STRICT (SPEC-0093 rule 6): reason + compensating_control + a real-ISO-date

 reason: "Initialized via `bin/yitc-v2 init` — no project-specific security-audit cadence yet; declare `cadence:` + `freshness_sla:` + `runner:` once this project has a security surface (SPEC-0145)."

profile_snapshot:
 # PROFILE SNAPSHOT (SPEC-0198, delivered by for the SPEC-0145 report).
 # ACTIVE AT BIRTH — and there is no stance here for you to take. The security-audit report
 # annotates itself with this project's DERIVED growth profile — `snapshot_hash` +
 # `check_set_hash` + the derived check set — so a report can be told apart from one produced
 # under a different risk profile. You do NOT maintain the profile: the kernel derives it from
 # this checkout and its journal (read it any time with `__YITC_CLI__ profile`).
 #
 # `command:` below is NOT an answer you were asked for — it is a DERIVED VALUE the kernel
 # RENDERS at init: the route from a byte-copied producer (no `bin/lib/` beside it) to the ONE
 # derivation site, `bin/lib/profile.py#resolve_profile`. A derived value is never asked as a
 # question (SPEC-0198), so a section whose every value is kernel-rendered is ratified BY
 # CONSTRUCTION and owes no unratified-adoption debt (SPEC-0119 rule 13's narrow exclusion).
 #
 # TO OPT OUT: replace `command:` with a `waiver:` whose `reason:` says why. The report is then
 # byte-identical to an unannotated one. A DECLARED-BUT-BROKEN command is never silent: the
 # report degrades VISIBLY, carrying `profile_snapshot.status: unavailable` plus an open
 # `SEC-PROFILE-SNAPSHOT` finding — so a broken declaration can never be mistaken for that
 # deliberate opt-out.

 # # consumes this mapping.
 # release: <the release tag the installed content was cut from>
 # answers: <OPTIONAL — where this project keeps its own init answers, if it keeps any, or ~;
 # no update reads it>
 #
 # THE REF IS EXACT AND IMMUTABLE, never a moving one. A release TAG is resolved to its PEELED
 # COMMIT and the bytes read are that commit's — a branch name is REFUSED, and a tag that does
 # not exist in `release_repo:` is a LOUD `pin-unresolved`, never a silent fall-through to
 # whatever engine happened to invoke the command. That silence is exactly what rule 4 retires:
 # `-C <project>` resolves the engine FROM this pin, not from an absolute host path baked into
 # a launcher, a doc, or a default.
 #
 # THE BORN STANCE IS A WAIVER, and it is a real key rather than commentary (the
 # lesson, `lessons/a-stance-mirror-is-only-sound-at-birth.md`): this section is EMITTED for
 # every project, so it is PRESENT — and a comment-only block declares NOTHING, so under
 # declare-or-waive every freshly-`init`ed project would fail its own born template.
 waiver:
 reason: >-
 Initialized via `bin/yitc-v2 init` — no pinned kernel release yet; this project runs the
 engine it was invoked with, from the
 workshop it lives beside. Replace this waiver with `engine: {release_repo, release}` once a
 release is published and this project installs from the artifact rather than the shared
 filesystem (SPEC-0195 rules 3-4).

overrides:
 # SPEC-0196 — THE OVERRIDE LEDGER: the ONLY sanctioned form of local divergence from an
 # upstream-owned file of the pinned release (the release contract's ownership classes). Born EMPTY, which is the
 # honest default: a fresh project diverges from nothing. Add an entry ONLY when this project
 # must run a local edit of an upstream-owned file before upstream carries it.
 #
 # Each entry carries EXACTLY these four fields (rule 1) — no others, no free-form policy text:
 # path: the upstream-owned file diverged from
 # rationale: one plain sentence — why this project needs the divergence now
 # upstream_intent: temporary-patch | forwarded | accepted-exception | not-forwarded
 # (a CLOSED vocabulary; `not-forwarded` is a recorded decision, never a default)
 # review_trigger: an ISO date (YYYY-MM-DD) OR a named artifact whose close re-opens the entry
 #
 # DELETE-ON-MERGE (rule 4): the moment the pinned release carries the divergence, delete the
 # entry AND drop the local edit — the drift check reports the entry REDUNDANT until you do.
 # The check is REPORT-ONLY and adds no land gate; it rides `update`'s divergence report and the
 # nightly sweep. An UNREGISTERED edit of an upstream-owned file is a CONFLICT on update and is
 # never resolved silently in either direction (rule 3).
